gitCommit.subject: Adopt the Rails 8.1 framework defaults
gitCommit.body:
Adopt the Rails 8.1 framework defaults

Separate commit from the gem upgrade on purpose: these are what change runtime
behaviour, so a regression here should be unambiguous about which half caused it.

All six of the 8.1 defaults were checked against this codebase rather than
adopted on faith:

- escape_json_responses = false. Read only at renderers.rb:171, inside the
  controller JSON renderer. Object#to_json in views is governed by a separate
  setting (escape_html_entities_in_json) that 8.1 does not touch, so the
  <script> tags in blog/show and dashboard/index are unaffected. The API is
  consumed by React Native and fetch, never injected into HTML.
- escape_js_separators_in_json = false. U+2028/2029 have been legal inside JS
  string literals since ES2019.
- raise_on_missing_required_finder_order_columns = true. Only raises for models
  with no order column at all; nothing in db/schema.rb declares id: false, so
  every table has a primary key to fall back on.
- action_on_path_relative_redirect = :raise. No redirect_to without a leading
  slash anywhere in app/controllers, and this closes an open-redirect class of
  bug rather than risking one.
- render_tracker = :ruby. Template dependency tracking, dev and test only.
- remove_hidden_field_autocomplete = true. Markup-only; no spec asserted on it.

No new_framework_defaults_8_1.rb. That file exists to flip these one at a time
over weeks; having checked all six against the code there is nothing left for it
to stage, and leaving it behind is a config layer someone has to clean up later.

Suite: 2971 examples, 0 failures, and zero deprecation warnings across the run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
